Data Understanding & EDA (15%)
(OLR AIT ///)
-Descriptive statistics
-Visualizations
-Relationship analysis
-Identification of key data issues (missing values, duplicates, outliers, imbalance, …)
-Interpretation of findings
Does not meet (0-1): Minimal or no EDA. Plots/stats shown without interpretation. Major issues ignored.
Nearly meets (2): Some plots/stats; superficial analysis; misses key insights
Meets (3-4): Solid EDA covering most of the above. Major issues identified and discussed.
Exceeds (5): Comprehensive EDA with clear insights. Subtler issues identified. Visuals well-presented and explained.

Implementation & Data Pipeline (20%)
(OLR AIT ///)
-Preprocessing and cleaning
-Feature engineering
-Leakage guards
-Integration of model(s) into a full pipeline
-Reproduciblility
Does not meet (0-1): Pipeline broken or missing major components
Nearly meets (2): Pipeline exists but fragile. Preprocessing flawed or misuses libraries.
Meets (3-4): Functional end-to-end pipeline. Preprocessing correctly applied. Minor reproducibility issues.
Exceeds (5): Clean, modular, reproducible pipeline. Good practices (clear code, logical workflow). Well-documented workflow.

column1:
Model Selection & Justification (15%)
(OLR AIT ///)
(OLR AIT ///)
-Choice of algorithm(s) appropriate for the problem (including baselines and candidates)
- Hyperparameter Tuning
-Comparison of multiple models
-Justification of choices
Does not meet (0-1):
No valid model, or arbitrary choice with no reasoning.
No HPT attempted or HPT misapplied
Nearly meets (2): Model selected but poorly justified. Little awareness of alternatives. Minimal tuning, no explanation.
Meets (3-4): Appropriate model chosen. Reasoning clear. Some alternatives considered. Basic HPT performed.
Exceeds (5): Multiple models compared systematically. Strong justification, with awareness of assumptions and trade-offs. Thoughtful HPT process.

column1:
Evaluation  & Analysis (20%)
(OLR AIT ///)
(OLR AIT ///)
-Correct evaluation metrics chosen
-Sound validation strategy (train/val/test split, cross-validation)
-Visualise the results
-Correct interpretation of results
-Critical reflection on model strenghts and weaknesses (e.g., performance, limitations, risks, fairness, bias)
Does not meet (0-1): No evaluation, or metrics/validation clearly wrong
Nearly meets (2): Some metrics, but inappropriate or shallow. Little interpretation.
Meets (3-4): Correct metrics and validation. Results interpreted reasonably. Some reflection on limitations/bias.
Exceeds (5): Thorough evaluation with appropriate metrics and validation. Deep interpretation of results. Possibly reflection on risks, fairness, and ethical use.

Individual Oral Defense (30%)
(OLR AIT ///)
(OLR AIT ///)
-Student explains their personal contributions
-Demonstrates understanding of code and decisions
-Ability to handle “what if” questions
-Ability to adapt reasoning to new but related scenarios
-Awareness of the full ML lifecycle
Does not meet (0-1): Cannot explain own contributions, little understanding of code
Nearly meets (2): Explains some contributions and choices, but with gaps or limited depth; struggles to answer follow-up questions
Meets (3-4): Explains contributions clearly, demonstrates understanding of pipeline/choices
Exceeds (5): Explains deeply, anticipates questions, demonstrates broad awareness of ML lifecycle, can reason in new scenarios.

column1:
Deployment (+5% Bonus; only if ML lifecyle steps ≥ Meets)
(OLR AIT ///)
-Students expose their trained model as an API
-Should accept input data, return predictions in a usable format
-Doesn’t need to be production-ready (Docker, CI/CD, cloud, …)
-Must be demonstrated live (e.g., curl, Postman)
Does not meet (0-1): API deployment doesn't work or is missing
Exceeds (5): API deployment works and is demonstrated
